saints.name: Pope St. Celestine I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope who upheld the title Mother of God at Ephesus and sent the faith toward Britain and Ireland…
biography: A Roman deacon under Innocent I, Celestine was elected bishop of Rome in 422. His ten-year pontificate was a sustained defence of the inherited faith: he curbed the Novatians at Rome, insisting that pardon never be refused to a dying sinner who sincerely asked it, and continued the condemnation of Pelagian teaching on grace.

Above all he moved against Nestorius of Constantinople, whose preaching denied Mary the title Theotokos, Mother of God. A Roman synod in 430 condemned the error, and Celestine commissioned Cyril of Alexandria to act in his name; the next year his legates joined the Council of Ephesus, which upheld the title.

His care reached the ends of the Christian world: he sent Germanus of Auxerre to Britain in 429 against Pelagianism and, in 431, the deacon Palladius as first bishop to the believing Scots of Ireland, before St. Patrick. He died in 432 and was buried on the Via Salaria; his body now rests in Santa Prassede at Rome.
saints.knownFor: Backing the Council of Ephesus and the defence of Mary as Mother of God.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 6 April
